introduction.en: The Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) was established under the RBI Act, 1934, to bring transparency and accountability to monetary policy decisions. It is tasked with maintaining price stability while keeping in mind the objective of growth.
introduction.hi: The Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) was established under the RBI Act, 1934, to bring transparency and accountability to monetary policy decisions. It is tasked with maintaining price stability while keeping in mind the objective of growth.

body.en: The MPC uses the inflation targeting framework, aiming for 4% CPI inflation with a tolerance band of +/- 2%. When inflation exceeds the target, the MPC adopts a hawkish stance by increasing the repo rate to reduce liquidity and demand. Conversely, to support growth during a slowdown, it adopts an accommodative stance by lowering rates to stimulate investment and consumption.

conclusion.en: By balancing these dual objectives, the MPC plays a critical role in ensuring macroeconomic stability, which is essential for sustainable long-term economic growth in India.

overview.title: Monetary Policy
overview.definition: Monetary policy refers to the macroeconomic policy implemented by the central bank (RBI in India) to manage the money supply, interest rates, and overall liquidity in the economy to achieve price stability while keeping in mind economic growth.
overview.importanceInUpsc: Crucial for both Prelims (direct policy rates, tools, MPC composition, liquidity management) and Mains GS Paper III (Indian Economy, inflation control, central bank autonomy, financial inclusion).
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Monetary Policy.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
prerequisites: Core foundational concepts of banking, inflation, and macroeconomics

sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Statutory Basis**: Governed by the **Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934** (Section 45ZB amended in 2016).
• **Primary Objective**: Maintenance of **price stability** while keeping in mind the objective of **growth**.
• **Inflation Targeting Framework**: Adopted in 2016 based on the **Urjit Patel Committee Report**. The target is **4% CPI inflation** with a tolerance band of **+/- 2%** (Upper tolerance: 6%, Lower tolerance: 2%).
• **Monetary Policy Committee (MPC)**: A 6-member statutory body responsible for fixing the benchmark policy interest rate (Repo Rate).

items.definition: The interest rate at which the RBI lends money to commercial banks against government securities.
A collateral-free liquidity absorption tool introduced in 2022 to absorb excess liquidity from commercial banks without needing government securities.
A window for scheduled banks to borrow overnight funds from RBI against approved government securities up to a limit (typically 2-3% of NDTL) at a rate higher than the repo rate.

items.title: Major Geographical Distribution / Regional Hubs
items.content:
• **Financial Transmission Hubs**: Mumbai (HQ of RBI and major scheduled commercial banks), National Capital Region (Policy formulation and central regulatory bodies).
• **Rural-Urban Disparity**: Monetary policy transmission is often asymmetric; urban credit responds faster to rate cuts compared to rural cooperative and microfinance networks.

items.title: Challenges, Reforms & Forward Strategy
items.content:
• **Bottlenecks / Issues**: Sluggish monetary transmission, twin balance sheet problem, sticky core inflation, and global spillovers (Fed rate hikes).
• **Policy Interventions**: Introduction of External Benchmark Lending Rate (EBLR) linked to Repo Rate to quicken transmission, digital currency (e-Rupee) integration.

items.title: Mnemonic for MPC Composition
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym / Phrase**: '3 + 3 = RBI'
• **Decoded Meaning**: 3 officials from RBI (Governor, Deputy Governor, Executive Director) + 3 external members appointed by the Central Government.
• **Prelims Exam Value**: Instantly verifies questions regarding the structural parity of the MPC.

items.title: Retention Rule of Thumb
items.content: • **Core Formula / Rule**: 'Tight policy cuts inflation, Loose policy pumps growth' — Whenever inflation crosses the 6% upper band for 3 consecutive quarters, RBI must explain its failure to the Central Government.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC frequently states that the Finance Minister or the Prime Minister decides the Repo Rate or chairs the MPC. Remember: The RBI Governor chairs the MPC, and the Finance Minister has no direct say in setting policy rates.

Mains Value Addition: Discuss the 'Trilemma of International Finance' (impossible to have a fixed exchange rate, free capital movement, and independent monetary policy simultaneously) when answering questions on macroeconomic stability.

keyTakeaways: Monetary policy in India operates under a statutory Flexible Inflation Targeting framework centered around 4% CPI inflation.
The 6-member Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) balances growth and price stability using quantitative tools like Repo, SDF, MSF, CRR, and SLR.
Effective monetary policy transmission requires structural reforms in the banking sector and seamless pass-through of repo rate changes to end borrowers.
